mutations.rationale: P3 positive control: the native NULLS FIRST arm of RenderNative. Stryker mutant id 10263 ('String mutation' -> '') reports exactly this span, 68:36-68:50, and the hand-applied P3 edit measured 8 failed / 4 passed of the 12 scoped tests, then restored 12/12. 1-based column 36 is the opening quote, so the byte-anchored find carries the quotes; the literal value is ' NULLS FIRST'. Expected: KILLED (the flipped cell is asserted at T287NullOrderingTests.cs:97 and the same fragment reaches the native, parameterized, index, then-by, paging, distinct, distinct-on, per-parent-rank and extreme-row tests).

Escape control in the only non-native render path: the CASE-emulation template of NullsOrderingRenderer.Render (line 52). Every NULL placement is emitted through _ctx.Dialect.RenderOrderBy (SqlBuilder.cs:883 rank window, :902 occurrences, :1609), and PostgreSQL overrides that member with RenderNative + SupportsNullsOrdering => true (PostgresDialect.cs:92,96); the base/interface implementations (SqlDialectBase.cs:137, ISqlDialect.cs:404) that reach Render are therefore unreachable for a Postgres context. All 12 scoped tests build their SQL from PostgresTestContext.Create(), and three of them assert the emitted SQL does NOT contain 'CASE' (T287NullOrderingTests.cs:106,308,346) - a guard that only holds while the emulation is bypassed. Replacing the emulation keyword with a visibly different token is hence unobservable by the cohort. Expected: ESCAPED (this is what proves the harness does not kill mutations the scoped tests cannot reach).
